questions.question: The function g is defined by g(x) = −8x + 60. What is the value of g(x) when x = −3?
If 5c = 15, what is the value of 5c − 8?

Sarah used wax to make candles. The function f(x) = −12x + 60 approximates the weight, in ounces, of wax Sarah had remaining after making x candles. Which statement is the best interpretation of the y-intercept of the graph of y = f(x) in the xy-plane in this context?
options: Sarah used approximately 12 ounces of wax for each candle.
Sarah had approximately 12 ounces of wax when she began to make the candles.
Sarah had approximately 60 ounces of wax when she began to make the candles.
Sarah used approximately 60 ounces of wax for each candle.
questions.explanation: The y-intercept (0, 60) means that before any candles were made, Sarah had about 60 ounces of wax.

questions.question: A soccer team's goal is to earn at least $1,320 by selling coupon books. The team earns $12 from selling each coupon book. Which of the following inequalities describes all possible values for the number of coupon books, n, the team can sell to meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Earnings 12n must be at least 1,320, so 12n ≥ 1,320.

questions.question:
3x = 45y − 27
One of the two equations in a system of linear equations is given. The system has no solution. Which equation could be the second equation in this system?
questions.explanation: The given equation simplifies to x = 15y − 9. Choice B simplifies to x = 15y, a parallel line with a different intercept, so the system has no solution.

questions.question: If 9 − 6(3 − 4x) = 6 − 7(3 − 4x), what is the value of 3 − 4x?
questions.explanation: Let t = 3 − 4x. Then 9 − 6t = 6 − 7t, so t = −3.

questions.question: For groups of 25 or more people, a museum charges $21 per person for the first 25 people and $14 for each additional person. Which function f gives the total charge, in dollars, for a tour group with n people, where n ≥ 25?

√(x2) = 24 − 5x
What is the solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: √(x²) = |x|. If x ≥ 0, x = 24 − 5x gives x = 4. If x < 0, −x = 24 − 5x gives x = 6, which is not negative, so x = 4 is the only solution.

questions.question:
f(x) = √5x + 6
The function f is defined by the given equation. If f(a) = −5a, where a is a constant, what is the value of a?
Which expression is equivalent to (3x<sup>3</sup> − x<sup>2</sup> + 4)(5x<sup>2</sup> + 8x)?
questions.explanation: Expanding gives 15x⁵ + 24x⁴ − 5x⁴ − 8x³ + 20x² + 32x = 15x⁵ + 19x⁴ − 8x³ + 20x² + 32x.

questions.question:
The functions f and g are defined by the given equations, where x ≥ 0, a and b are integer constants, a < b, and a > 1. If y = f(x) and y = g(x) are graphed in the xy−plane, which of the following equations displays, as a constant or coefficient, the minimum value of the function it defines, where x ≥ 0?
I. f(x) = a(0.63)(−bx)
II. g(x) = a(1.37)(x+2) + b
questions.explanation: Since 0.63^(−bx) = (1/0.63)^(bx) is increasing, f has its minimum at x = 0, equal to a, which appears as the coefficient. For g the minimum is a(1.37)^2 + b, which is not displayed.

questions.question: The function f is defined by f(x) = ab(x/n), where a, b, and n are constants, and b and n are integers. If f(2) = 6 and f(5) = 162, what is the value of f(7)?

A quadratic function models the height, in feet, of an object above the ground in terms of the time, in seconds, after the object is launched off an elevated surface. The model indicates the object has an initial height of 2 feet above the ground and reaches its maximum height of 258 feet above the ground 4 seconds after being launched. Based on the model, what is the height, in feet, of the object above the ground 5 seconds after being launched?

r + g < 56
For which of the following tables are all the values of r and their corresponding values of g solutions to the given inequality?
questions.explanation: In table A every pair sums to 55, which is less than 56. In each other table some pair sums to 57 or more.

questions.question: A certain goose species can fly at an average speed of 16 meters per second when in continuous flight. At this rate, how many meters would this goose species fly in 6 seconds?
questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 16 × 6 = 96 meters.

The table shows values of x and their corresponding values of y for three points on line j in the xy−plane. Line k also lies in the xy−plane and is defined by the equation y = 4x. At what point (x, y) do lines j and k intersect?
questions.explanation: Line j has slope 6 and y-intercept −10: y = 6x − 10. Setting 6x − 10 = 4x gives x = 5, y = 20.

questions.question: James purchased a certain baseball card on January 1. The function f(x) = 55(1.04)<sup>x</sup>, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 10, gives the predicted value, in dollars, of the baseball card x years after James purchased it. What is the best interpretation of the statement “f(7) is approximately equal to 72” in this context?
options: When the baseball card’s predicted value is approximately 72 dollars, it is 7% greater than the predicted value, in dollars, on January 1 of the previous year.
When the baseball card’s predicted value is approximately 72 dollars, it is 7 times the predicted value, in dollars, on January 1 of the previous year.
From the day James purchased the baseball card to 7 years after James purchased the card, its predicted value increased by a total of approximately 72 dollars.
7 years after James purchased the baseball card, its predicted value is approximately 72 dollars.
questions.explanation: f(7) is the predicted value 7 years after purchase, so D (55 · 1.04⁷ ≈ 72.4).

questions.question: For the positive quantities h, j, and k, 27% of h is equivalent to 24% of j, and j is equivalent to 45% of k. What percentage of k is h? (Disregard the % sign when entering your answer. For example, if your answer is 39%, enter 39)

Note: Figure not drawn to scale.

What is the value of cos A in the triangle shown?
questions.explanation: The right angle is at C, so cos A = adjacent/hypotenuse = AC/AB = 31/32.

questions.question: In right triangle ABC, angles A and B are acute, side AC has a length of 21.7, and tanB = 18. What is the length of side BC, rounded to the nearest tenth?
Cube B has a volume of 216 cubic inches. The length of each edge of cube A is k times the length of each edge of cube B. If cube A has a volume of 5,832 cubic inches, what is the value of k?
questions.explanation: Cube B has edge 6 inches and cube A has edge the cube root of 5,832, which is 18 inches. So k = 18/6 = 3.

questions.question: In right triangle RST, the sum of the measures of angle R and angle S is 90 degrees. The value of sin(R) is 4√29. What is the value of cos(S)?
questions.explanation: R and S are complementary, so cos(S) = sin(R) = 4√2/9.

questions.question:
((x − 4)(x − 8))/(x − 1) = 0
What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.explanation: The fraction is zero when the numerator is zero and the denominator is not: x = 4 or x = 8. Their sum is 12.

2x + y = −2

questions.topic: Systems of two linear equations in two variables

questions.question: In the xy-plane, line k has a slope of 5 and a y-intercept of (0, −35). What is the x-coordinate of the x-intercept of line k?
questions.explanation: y = 5x − 35 = 0 gives x = 7.

questions.question: If 67p + 42 = 84, what is the value of 7p?

The graph gives the estimated population y, in thousands, of a town x years since 2001, where 0 ≤ x ≤ 5. Which of the following best describes the increase in the estimated population from x = 0 to x = 1?
options: The estimated population at x = 1 is 0.5 times the estimated population at x = 0.
The estimated population at x = 1 is 1.5 times the estimated population at x = 0.
The estimated population at x = 1 is 2.5 times the estimated population at x = 0.
The estimated population at x = 1 is 3.5 times the estimated population at x = 0.
questions.explanation: The graph starts at about 5 at x = 0 and is about 7.5 at x = 1, a ratio of 1.5.

questions.question: −x − wy = −357 and 2x − wy = 51. In the given system of equations, w is a constant. In the xy-plane, the graphs of these equations intersect at the point (q, 17), where q is a constant. What is the value of w?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the equations gives 3x = 408, so q = 136. Then −136 − 17w = −357, so w = 13.

questions.question: A freight elevator can hold a maximum weight of 5,450 pounds during one trip. A 190-pound person needs to deliver several boxes using the freight elevator. Some of these boxes weigh 23 pounds each and the others weigh 60 pounds each. Which inequality represents the possible combinations of the number of 23-pound boxes, x, and the number of 60-pound boxes, y, the person can deliver during one trip if only the person and the boxes are on the freight elevator?
questions.explanation: Total weight 190 + 23x + 60y must be at most 5,450, so 23x + 60y ≤ 5,260.

questions.question: The variables x and y have a quadratic relationship. When x = 0, y = 45. When x = 6, y = 81. When x = 15, y = 0. Which equation represents this relationship?
The graph gives the estimated revenue, in dollars, for a company when the price of the company's product is x dollars. What does the y-value of the vertex of the graph represent in this context?
options: The price, in dollars, of the company's product
The minimum estimated revenue, in dollars
The maximum estimated revenue, in dollars
The estimated revenue, in dollars, when the price of the company's product is 0 dollars
questions.explanation: The vertex is the highest point of the parabola, so its y-value is the maximum estimated revenue.

questions.question:
(x − k)2 = (k − 4a)(x − k)
In the given equation, a and k are constants, where k > 4a. The sum of the solutions to the equation is 3k + 35. What is the value of a?
questions.explanation: The solutions are x = k and x = 2k − 4a, so 3k − 4a = 3k + 35 and a = −35/4.

questions.question:
An acceptable noise criterion rating for the background noise in a school classroom is 30. For a noise criterion rating of 30, the equation

y = 19(0.978)x − 50 + 37

gives the estimated sound pressure level, y, in decibels, as a function of the octave band center frequency, x, in hertz, where x ≥ 50. Which of the following is the best interpretation of 37 in this context?
options: 37 is 19 less than the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 50
37 is 19 less than the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 0
37 is the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 50
37 is the estimated sound pressure level, in decibels, at an octave band frequency of 0

In the given equation, k is a constant. The solution to the given equation is 1174. What is the value of k?

A quadratic function models the height, in feet, of an object above the ground in terms of the time, in seconds, after the object was launched. According to the model, the object was launched from a height of 0 feet and reached its maximum height of 1,600 feet 10 seconds after it was launched. Based on the model, what was the height, in feet, of the object 7 seconds after it was launched?
On average, a certain tree grows 51 centimeters every m months. At this rate, which expression represents the number of centimeters, on average, the tree grows every k years?
questions.explanation: The rate is 51/m cm per month, and k years is 12k months: (51/m)(12k) = (612k)/(m).

questions.question: A car travels at a constant speed of 65 miles per hour. If the car consumes fuel at a rate of 25 miles per gallon, how many gallons of fuel are consumed when the car travels a distance of 325 miles?
questions.topic: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units

questions.question: A science club from a certain high school in Ohio conducted an experiment to study the effects of smell on taste. A sample of 125 students was selected at random from the high school to participate in the experiment. First, the students tasted a pureed food sample while wearing covered goggles and nose plugs. Then, the students tasted the same pureed food sample without nose plugs. 50 students were able to correctly identify the pureed food sample while wearing nose plugs. Which of the following is the largest population to which the results of the experiment can be generalized?
options: The 50 students who were able to correctly identify the pureed food sample while wearing nose plugs
All students from the high school
The 125 students who participated in the experiment
All students from high schools in Ohio
questions.explanation: The sample was random only within this one high school, so results generalize to all students at that school and no further.

questions.question: In triangle FGH and triangle KLM, the measures of angles G and L are each 30°. The lengths of GH and LM are each 34 centimeters, and GH/GF = LM/LK. Which additional piece of information would be necessary to prove that triangle FGH is congruent to triangle KLM?
options: The lengths of FG and KM are each 17 centimeters.
The measures of angles H and M are each 60°.
The measures of angles F and K are each 90°.
questions.explanation: Since GH = LM, the ratio gives GF = LK. Two sides and the included angle are equal (SAS), so the triangles are congruent.

questions.question: The circumference of the base of a right circular cylinder is 6π meters, and the height of the cylinder is 19 meters. What is the volume, in cubic meters, of the cylinder?
questions.explanation: 2πr = 6π gives r = 3, so V = π(3)^2(19) = 171π.

questions.question:
(x + 3)2 + (y − 18)2 = 169
The graph of the given equation is a circle in the xy-plane. The point (a, b) lies on the circle. Which of the following is a possible value for a?
questions.explanation: The circle has center (−3, 18) and radius 13, so a must be between −16 and 10. Only −12 is in that range.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, the measure of angle A is 56° and AC = 35. In triangle PQR, the measure of angle P is 56° and PR = 105. Which additional piece of information is sufficient to prove that triangle ABC is similar to triangle PQR?
options: The measures of angle B and angle R are 32° and 92°, respectively.
The measures of angle B and angle Q are 56° and 32°, respectively.
questions.explanation: If B = 32° then C = 180° − 56° − 32° = 92° = R, so angles A = P and C = R match and the triangles are similar by AA.

questions.question: The perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 876 centimeters. The three vertices of the triangle lie on a circle. The radius of the circle is w√3 centimeters. What is the value of w?
questions.explanation: Each side is 876 ÷ 3 = 292. The circumradius of an equilateral triangle is s/√3 = 292√3/3, so w = 292/3 ≈ 97.33.
